examples.en: I trembled while watching a scary movie.
I'm so cold my whole body is shaking.
My hands trembled before the presentation.

examples.ko: 아이가 개를 보고 벌벌 떨면서 울었어요.
examples.en: The child saw a dog, shook with fear, and cried.

examples.ko: 선생님 앞에서 벌벌 떨 필요 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to shake in front of the teacher.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에 올라가니까 다리가 벌벌 떨려요!
examples.en: My legs are shaking since I climbed up somewhere high!

explain: '벌벌'은 무섭거나 추워서 몸이 떠는 모양을 말해요. 늘 '떨다', '떨리다'와 함께 쓰고 '벌벌 떨다'가 하나의 덩어리예요. '덜덜'은 추위나 기계에, '부들부들'은 화나거나 힘줄 때 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: The dog shakes in fear at the sound of thunder.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌벌'이 가장 자주 붙는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic and common form with 벌벌.

phrases.en: My hands were shaking before the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 몸이 저절로 떨릴 때는 '떨리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 떨리다 when your body shakes on its own.

phrases.en: He opened the door, trembling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨면서 다른 행동을 할 때 '-면서'로 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -면서 to connect another action done while trembling.

explain_en: Shaking from fear or nerves; spoken, repeated trembling. 벌벌 shows a body shaking from fear or cold, and it is nearly always used with 떨다 or 떨리다 as 벌벌 떨다. 덜덜 fits cold or machines better, and 부들부들 fits anger or strain.

t90.ax: I'm so cold my whole body is shaking.

en: to worry; to bother; to keep someone in suspense

examples.en: I was anxious all day because I didn't hear from them.

examples.ko: 그만 애태우고 결과를 빨리 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Stop keeping me in suspense and tell me the result already.
Don't keep your parents worried for too long.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 답장을 늦게 해서 저를 애태워요.
examples.en: He replies late on purpose to keep me on edge.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리며 애태우던 시간이 길었어요.
examples.en: The time I spent anxiously waiting for my exam results was long.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 앞두고 애태우는 친구를 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: I comforted my friend who was fretting before the pass announcement.

explain: '걱정하다'보다 속이 타고 조마조마한 느낌이 훨씬 강해요. 내가 혼자 마음을 졸일 때도 쓰고, 위 예문처럼 남을 애태우게 할 때도 써요. 말할 때는 '애를 태우다'라고 띄어서 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I'm anxious waiting for my exam results.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애태우다'를 띄어 쓴 말하기 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of the word, common in speech.
phrases.en_equiv: to fret; to be on edge

phrases.en: I'm eaten up with worry about my son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 걱정으로 마음이 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar phrase used when worry hurts inside.
phrases.en_equiv: to be eaten up with worry

phrases.en: I waited anxiously for the news of my acceptance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조마조마한 마음으로 기다릴 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for waiting with a nervous heart.

explain_en: Restless, anxious waiting; also making someone anxious; expressive. It is much stronger than '걱정하다': it carries a feeling of being on pins and needles. You can use it when you fret alone, or, as in the examples, when you make someone else anxious. People also say it as two words, '애를 태우다'.

t90.ax: Don't keep your parents worried for too long.

en: to despair; to lose all hope

examples.en: Don't despair just because you failed the exam.
He fell into despair when he heard the news of the accident.
Despairing alone won't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 절망하는 친구에게 따뜻한 말을 해 줬어요.
examples.en: I said kind words to my friend who was in despair.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 잃고 절망한 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people had lost everything and despaired.
There's no need to despair so early.

explain: 절망하다는 희망이 완전히 없다고 느낄 때 써요. 그냥 '실망하다'는 기대와 달라서 마음이 상하는 정도이고, 절망하다는 훨씬 더 깊고 무거운 말이에요. '절망하지 마세요'처럼 위로할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 실패 후 절망에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: He fell into despair after a big failure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '절망'과 함께 깊은 슬픈 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 절망 for a deep state of sadness.

phrases.en: He came home with a despairing face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표정이나 모습을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a facial look or appearance.

phrases.en: Even when it's hard, I don't despair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포기하지 않는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to show you keep hope.

explain_en: Hope is completely gone, a very heavy feeling. 절망하다 is used when you feel there is no hope left at all. '실망하다' is being let down because things didn't match your expectations, while 절망하다 is much deeper and heavier. A common use is comforting someone: '절망하지 마세요'.

t90.ax: There's no need to despair so early.

en: to be admirable; to be respectable

examples.ko: 어려운 일을 끝까지 하는 모습이 존경스러워요.
examples.en: The way you see hard things through is admirable.
I met a teacher I admire.
His words and actions were admirable.

examples.ko: 아무도 안 보는데 약속을 지키니까 존경스럽네요.
examples.en: You keep your promise even when no one is watching; that's admirable.
My grandmother's life is so admirable that I bowed my head.

examples.ko: 매일 봉사하는 이웃이 존경스러울 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I find the neighbor who volunteers every day admirable.

explain: '~을 존경하다'는 대상을 '을/를'로 받지만 '~이/가 존경스럽다'는 대상이 '이/가'로 와요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '존경스러워요', '존경스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 그 사람을 보고 저절로 드는 느낌을 말해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is a truly admirable person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 닮고 싶은 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, used for a person you look up to.

phrases.en: The way you volunteer every day is admirable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅂ' 불규칙 형용사라서 '존경스럽다'가 '존경스러워요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a 'ㅂ' irregular adjective, so '존경스럽다' becomes '존경스러워요'.

phrases.example: 그분은 늘 열심히 일해서 존경스럽게 보여요.
phrases.en: That person always works hard, so they look admirable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 행동을 보고 느끼는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the feeling comes from how someone looks or acts.

explain_en: Deep respect felt toward a teacher or elder; suitable for superiors. '존경하다' marks its object with '을/를', but with '존경스럽다' the person admired takes '이/가'. It is a 'ㅂ' irregular, so it becomes '존경스러워요' and '존경스러운'. It describes the feeling that arises on seeing that person.

t90.ax: I met a teacher I admire.

examples.ko: 친구가 칭찬받는 걸 보고 질투심이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I felt jealous when I saw my friend get praised.

examples.ko: 질투심 때문에 그 사람과 말도 하기 싫었어요.
examples.en: Out of jealousy, I didn't even want to talk to that person.

examples.ko: 동생은 질투심이 강해서 장난감을 나눠 쓰지 않아요.
examples.en: My little brother is very jealous, so he won't share his toys.
I laughed on purpose to hide my jealousy.

examples.ko: 그는 질투심에 눈이 멀어 친구를 의심했어요.
examples.en: Blinded by jealousy, he suspected his friend.

examples.ko: 작은 질투심은 사랑하는 사이에서 자주 생겨요.
examples.en: A little jealousy often comes up between people in love.

explain: '질투심이 생기다', '질투심이 강하다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '시기'는 남이 잘되는 걸 싫어하는 마음이고, 질투심은 사랑하는 사람이나 내 것을 빼앗길까 불안한 마음에도 써요. 사람을 말할 때는 '질투가 많다'도 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그는 질투심이 강해서 친구의 성공을 기뻐하지 못해요.
phrases.en: He is very jealous, so he can't be happy about his friend's success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격으로 질투를 잘하는 사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who is jealous by nature.

phrases.example: 저는 친구의 새 가방이 부러워서 질투했어요.
phrases.en: I envied my friend's new bag and felt jealous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '질투심'의 동사형이라 행동이나 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used for the action or feeling.

phrases.en: I felt jealous because my younger sibling got praised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 질투하는 마음이 생길 때 대화에서 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural in conversation when jealousy suddenly rises.

explain_en: Common patterns are 질투심이 생기다 and 질투심이 강하다. 시기 is resenting someone else's success, while 질투심 also covers the anxiety of losing someone you love or something you have. For a person, 질투가 많다 is also natural.

t90.ax: I laughed on purpose to hide my jealousy.

en: to remember; to recall; to look back

examples.en: I sometimes think fondly of my school days.
I looked at old photos with my friends and reminisced.
Grandmother smiled as she looked back on her youth.
That song makes me recall last summer.

examples.ko: 우리는 같이 여행한 날을 추억하곤 해요.
examples.en: We often look back on the day we traveled together.
I'm happy because I have a lot to look back on.

explain: '추억하다'는 좋았던 옛날을 따뜻하게 떠올릴 때 써요. 나쁜 기억에는 보통 쓰지 않아요. 일상 대화에서는 '그때가 생각나요', '추억이 있어요'처럼 명사 '추억'을 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: We talked with friends, remembering old times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날을 떠올리면서 다른 일을 함께 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you do something while looking back on the past.

phrases.en: I sometimes look back on my childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추억하다'와 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요. 좋았던 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with '추억하다', usually for happy times.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날이면 그 여행을 추억하곤 해요.
phrases.en: On rainy days I often think back on that trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가끔 반복해서 떠올린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you recall it from time to time, repeatedly.

explain_en: Literary, nostalgic; looking back on the past with feeling (어린 시절을 추억하다). 추억하다 is for warmly recalling good times in the past, and is not usually used for bad memories. In daily talk people more often use the noun, as in '추억이 있어요' or '그때가 생각나요'.

dis.h: look back fondly on the past
gh: something comes to mind by itself

p.n: 추억하다 means looking back warmly. 기억하다 means plainly remembering.

examples.en: The child broke into a broad smile on getting the present.

examples.ko: 남자는 사진 속에서 청바지를 입고 함박웃음을 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: In the photo, the man is wearing jeans and smiling broadly.
Grandma welcomed me with a big, bright smile.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 엄마 얼굴에 함박웃음이 가득했어요.
examples.en: Mom's face was full of smiles at the news that I passed.
I saw a photo of my friends smiling broadly.
His big smile put me in a good mood too.

explain: '활짝 웃다'처럼 얼굴 전체로 크게 웃는 모습이 그려져요. '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'처럼 써요. 소리 내어 크게 웃는 '폭소'와는 달리 환하게 웃는 모습에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: The child came running with a big smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 환하게 웃는 얼굴을 보여 줄 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for showing a big, bright smile.

phrases.en: My sibling burst into a big smile when opening the gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 웃음이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a big smile suddenly breaks out.

phrases.example: 사진을 찍을 때 활짝 웃어 보세요.
phrases.en: Try smiling brightly when we take the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 느낌을 동사로 쉽게 말할 수 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy verb expression with a similar feeling.

explain_en: It paints a picture of a smile that lights up the whole face, like '활짝 웃다'. Use it as '함박웃음을 짓다/웃다/터뜨리다'. Unlike '폭소' (a burst of loud laughter), it is closer to a bright, beaming smile.

examples.en: The ancient history lesson started in history class.
Ancient history is hard but fun.
There is still much unknown in ancient history.

examples.ko: 고대사를 공부하려면 옛 기록을 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To study ancient history, you have to read old records.
My younger sibling is very interested in ancient history.
That scholar studies the secrets of ancient history.

explain: 한국사에서 '고대'는 보통 삼국 시대와 통일신라 무렵까지를 말해요. '중세사', '근대사', '현대사'와 나란히 시대를 나눌 때 써요. 학교 역사 수업과 교과서에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I'm very interested in ancient Korean history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어느 나라의 고대사인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a country name before it to say whose ancient history.

phrases.en: I'm studying ancient history at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문이나 전공을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about a subject or major.

phrases.en: I borrowed an ancient history book from the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고대사를 다룬 책이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book about ancient history.

explain_en: History of ancient times, as a subject (수업) In Korean history, 고대 usually means up to the Three Kingdoms and Unified Silla period. It is used alongside 중세사, 근대사, and 현대사 when dividing eras. It appears often in school history classes and textbooks.

examples.en: These days, domestic products are of very good quality too.
My grandmother tries to use only domestic products.
There's a poster urging people to use domestic products.
Domestic products are cheaper than foreign ones.
This shop specializes in domestic products.
I chose a domestic product as a gift.

explain: 우리나라에서 만든 물건을 말하고, 반대말은 '수입품'이에요. '국산품 애용'은 오래전부터 쓰던 표어 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '국산'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: This bag is made in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국산품'을 줄인 말로 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 국산품, used more in daily speech.

phrases.en: I use domestic products whenever I can.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애용하다'는 즐겨 자주 쓴다는 뜻이고, 오래된 표어에도 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 애용하다 means to use regularly; it also appears in old slogans.

phrases.en: I compared the prices of domestic and imported goods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '수입품'과 함께 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its opposite, 수입품.

explain_en: Made in one's own country, versus imported goods. It means goods made in Korea, and the opposite is '수입품'. '국산품 애용' is a long-used slogan-like phrase. In daily talk people often just say '국산'.

en: very first time; first time in one's life

examples.en: I rode an airplane for the first time in my life.
I went on a trip alone for the first time in my life.
It was food I had never seen before, so I was a bit scared.
I came first for the very first time and was really happy.

examples.ko: 저는 난생처음 김치를 직접 담가 봤어요.
examples.en: I made kimchi by myself for the first time in my life.

examples.ko: 난생처음 겪는 일이라 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: It was my first experience ever, so I didn't know what to do.

explain: 그냥 '처음'이 아니라 태어나서 지금까지 한 번도 없었다는 놀라움을 강조해요. 보통 '난생처음 + 동사'처럼 부사처럼 바로 동사 앞에 쓰고, '생전 처음'도 비슷하게 말해요.

phrases.en: I saw the sea for the first time in my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '난생처음'과 뜻은 같고, '으로'를 붙여 뒤의 동사와 이어서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '난생처음'; adding '으로' just links it to the verb that follows.
phrases.en_equiv: for the first time in my life

phrases.en: I wore a hanbok for the first time ever.
phrases.nuance_ko: '난생처음'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as the headword, common in speech.

phrases.en: It's my first time ever doing this, so I'm nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'와 함께 첫 경험을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '-아/어 보다' to talk about a first-time experience.
phrases.en_equiv: to try for the first time in one's life

explain_en: Rather than a plain 'first', it stresses surprise that this has never happened since you were born. It usually sits right before a verb like an adverb, and '생전 처음' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: When night fell, the neon lights on the street came on.
Myeongdong is full of flashy neon lights.
We made the shop name into a neon sign.
I took a photo under the neon lights.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 네온이 길에 비쳐서 예뻐요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the neon reflects on the road and looks pretty.

examples.ko: 저 가게 네온은 고장 났는지 깜빡거려요.
examples.en: The neon at that shop is flickering, maybe because it's broken.

explain: '네온'은 원래 기체 이름이지만 일상에서는 밤거리의 네온 불빛이나 간판을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 보통 '네온사인', '네온 간판'으로 더 자주 말해요. 불이 '켜지다', '꺼지다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The neon sign in front of the shop is sparkling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '네온'보다 더 자주 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common everyday word than plain 네온.

phrases.en: At night the neon signboards look very pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 이름을 알리는 간판일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is a signboard showing a shop's name.

phrases.en: When the sun sets, the neon lights come on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불빛은 '켜지다', '꺼지다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lights go with 켜지다 and 꺼지다.

explain_en: 네온 is originally the name of a gas, but in daily speech it usually means the glowing lights or signs seen on night streets. People more often say 네온사인 or 네온 간판. It goes with 켜지다 and 꺼지다.

t90.ax: I took a photo under the neon lights.

en: to rattle; to clatter; to clink

examples.en: Someone is clattering dishes in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 밤새 창문이 달그락거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The window rattled all night, so I couldn't sleep.
Mom is washing dishes with a clatter.
I can hear coins clinking in the pocket.
The keys in the drawer rattled.
Carry the dishes carefully so they don't clatter.

explain: 그릇, 숟가락, 동전처럼 작고 단단한 물건이 부딪히는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. '덜그럭거리다'는 좀 더 크고 무거운 느낌이에요. '달그락달그락'처럼 반복해서 소리를 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a clattering sound at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 '소리'를 붙여서 들린 소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'sound' lets you describe what you heard.

phrases.example: 동전이 가방 안에서 달그락달그락 소리가 나요.
phrases.en: The coins rattle in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 반복해서 흉내 내는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the repeated form that imitates the sound.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping, so please don't clatter the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone not to make that noise.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of small hard things like bowls, spoons or coins knocking together. '덜그럭거리다' feels a bit bigger and heavier. People also repeat it as '달그락달그락' to describe the sound.

t90.ax: The keys in the drawer rattled.

examples.en: At the top of the mountain I shouted "yahoo" loudly.
Yay! It's finally vacation!

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈을 보고 야호 하며 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: Seeing the snow, the kids ran out cheering.
The exam was over, so everyone cheered.
The shout echoed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 동생이 선물을 받고 야호 하고 좋아했어요.
examples.en: My little brother got a gift and cheered happily.

explain: '야호'는 기쁠 때 내는 소리이고, 특히 등산하다가 산 위에서 외치는 소리로 유명해요. 요즘은 산에서 소리를 지르는 것을 조심하라고 해서 예전만큼 많이 하지는 않아요. 기뻐서 외칠 때는 '앗싸'나 '만세'도 써요.

phrases.example: 친구들과 산 위에서 야호 하고 외쳤어요.
phrases.en: My friends and I shouted "yahoo" on top of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '야호'를 소리 내어 말할 때 '하고 외치다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '하고 외치다' to say someone shouted 야호 out loud.

phrases.en: Yay! There's no class today!
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 일이 생겼을 때 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual cheer for friends when something good happens.

phrases.en: Hooray! Our team won!
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 기뻐하며 두 손을 들 때 외치는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shouted with joy, often with both hands raised.

explain_en: 야호 is a sound of joy, and it is especially famous as the shout from a mountaintop while hiking. Today people are asked not to shout in the mountains, so it is done less than before. For a joyful cheer you can also say 앗싸 or 만세.
